title: Osiris Student Mobile
lists: The student can
construct and implement sophisticated numerical methods for ODE and DAE systems, and assess them in terms of accuracy and stability
apply dedicated methods for specific ODE systems, such as symplectic methods for Hamiltonian systems
implement and employ high performance parallelization techniques (MPI and GPU) for numerical methods for ODEs
identify and implement the most efficient HPC strategy based on the mathematical details of the use case
balance accuracy, high-performance, and object-orientation (for reuse) in advanced numerical software development
implement the cycle  Research question → Mathematics → Implementation → Simulation → Reflection

equations of motion, first order ODE system, initial conditions, initial value problem, differential-algebraic equations (DAEs), phase space, orbit/trajectory, flow, Hamiltonian system, classification of ODEs

basic integration methods, explicit/implicit Euler method, trapezoidal rule, implicit midpoint rule, Newton iteration, local discretisation error, consistency, global discretisation error, convergence

test equation, stability of numerical schemes, stability region, A- stability, upper bound for the global discretisation error, one-step methods for ODE-systems, stiff ODE systems, error estimate using Richardson extrapolation
derivation of Runge-Kutta methods, Butcher array, local discretisa- tion error, conditions for consistency, linear invariants.
Newton iteration for implicit Runge-Kutta methods, explicit Runge-Kutta methods, stability function, stability region, local error, step size control, local extrapolation, embedding.
Hamiltonian systems, (phase) flow, area preservation, symplectic mapping/flow, theorem of Poincaré.
symplectic time integration methods, symplectic Euler methods, implicit midpoint rule, symplectic Runge-Kutta methods, quadratic invariants, Störmer-Verlet scheme.

stiff ODE system, (linear) differential-algebraic equations (DAEs), consistent initial conditions, Weierstrass-Kronecker canonical form, general DAE, index, semi-explicit DAE, Hessenberg index-1/index-2 systems.
basic schemes for DAE systems, BDF methods, ODE system with invariants, stabilized ODE system.

examples of large-scale particle systems and applications (crowd, epidemiology, molecular), numerical implementation aspects of integrators: identification of the linear algebra operations (vector operations, matrix-vector op- erations, inner-product), linear update operator
basic consideration of parallelization, distributed vs shared memory computing architectures, MPI and GPU parallelization (vs hyperthreading) paradigms

Communication and Computation times, basic aspects of paral- lelization in different coding languages Python and Matlab, pros & cons, Matlab parallel programming toolbox, Python CuPy for Cuda-GPU, mpi4pi for MPI
domain partitioning and parallelization, truncation, communication vs computation time, scaling
specific considerations for the linear update operators, optimal strategies for large-scale applications

    Objectives

The student can
construct and implement sophisticated numerical methods for ODE and DAE systems, and assess them in terms of accuracy and stability
apply dedicated methods for specific ODE systems, such as symplectic methods for Hamiltonian systems
implement and employ high performance parallelization techniques (MPI and GPU) for numerical methods for ODEs
identify and implement the most efficient HPC strategy based on the mathematical details of the use case
balance accuracy, high-performance, and object-orientation (for reuse) in advanced numerical software development
implement the cycle  Research question → Mathematics → Implementation → Simulation → Reflection
